newsitem.title: INDIA: Two killed during elections in key Indian state.
newsitem.headline: Two killed during elections in key Indian state.

text.p: Two persons were killed in scattered violence as voters turned out for the second day of a three-stage local assembly poll in India's most populous Uttar Pradesh state on Thursday, officials said.
They said some 50 to 55 percent of voters, braving monsoon rains throughout the state, had cast their ballots in 160 constituencies at the close of polling on Thursday.
The elections in Uttar Pradesh began on September 30 and end on October 7.
"Despite sporadic violence, polling has been peaceful. Polling in only 40 out of 40,000 booths were affected by violence," G.B. Patnaik, state home (interior) secretary, told a news conference.
Poll officials said supporters of rival political parties clashed in at least eight places in the central and western regions of the sprawling state.
"Two people were killed in two separate clashes," said Noor Mohammad, chief electoral officer.

Officials said that activists of the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and a regional peasant party belonging to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's alliance clashed near Muzaffarnagar, 150 kms (90 miles) east of New Delhi.
In another clash between supporters of low-caste Samajwadi Party and BJP near Mainpuri, 250 km ( 156 miles) from Delhi, 14 BJP supporters were injured and admitted to a local hospital.
"Some 26 persons have been arrested at Mainpuri," Patnaik said.
Another party representing the lowest Hindu castes predicted on Thursday it would win the polls, regarded as crucial for Deve Gowda's government.
"We are heading for an outright victory to upset everyone's calculations," former Uttar Pradesh chief minister Mayawati told Reuters.

Mayawati said her Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), representing the Dalits, or former Hindu untouchables, would sweep the polls with the Congress party of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao as its junior partner.
Her prediction was at odds with recent opinion polls which have given an edge to the BJP, India's main opposition group that has made Uttar Pradesh its main base.
The government cancelled four of the 164 races in the fray on Thursday, three of them due to violence. Those elections will be held on October 9, two days after the scheduled final leg of the polls.
Tens of thousands of paramilitary troops have been deployed to guard the elections in the violence-prone state.
Police last week clamped an around-the-clock curfew in the Moslem-majority old quarter of Lucknow, the state capital and the main base of the BJP.

The assembly polls have Deve Gowda's fractious United Front alliance taking on the Congress party -- which supports his minority government in Delhi but is allied with the BSP in Uttar Pradesh -- and the BJP in a triangular fight for the state's 425-member Vidhan Sabha, or lower house.

Politicians said the polls, involving 90 million eligible voters, would test Deve Gowda's ability to ride out a challenge by the BJP, India's main opposition group, which is campaigning for mid-term parliamentary polls.
